subject.title: [Bug]: `openclaw models auth login` on node host writes OAuth token locally instead of syncing to gateway

question: Should remote node-host `models auth login` fail closed with an instruction to run on the gateway host, or should OpenClaw add a gateway credential-forwarding flow?
rationale: Both options prevent the wrong-host credential write, but forwarding OAuth credentials changes a security-sensitive gateway/auth surface while fail-closed changes existing CLI behavior for remote-node users.

options.title: Fail closed before auth
options.body: Block remote node-host auth login before starting provider auth, reuse shared loopback checks, and tell the user to run the command on the gateway host.

options.title: Design credential forwarding
options.body: Add an explicit gateway RPC or setup flow for credential transfer, with security review and upgrade proof before implementation.

options.title: Warn but allow
options.body: Emit a warning and still allow local writes, accepting that users can still consume OAuth credentials on the wrong host.

recommendation.title: Fail closed before auth
recommendation.body: Block remote node-host auth login before starting provider auth, reuse shared loopback checks, and tell the user to run the command on the gateway host.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current history and linked follow-up context for the auth-login/node-host boundary.
